theory ListProg

Lists as programs

Head, tail, membership, non-repetition, fold, and append — Constable et al. §11.2.

Constable et al. §11.2

Lists as a programming theory, following Constable et al. §11.2 (the Nuprl book’s “Lists and Arrays”).

A discrete type has decidable equality; a predicate is decidable when it or its negation holds at every point. Head is defined in two ways (partial vs. defaulted), tail and length by `list_ind`, membership and non-repetition as recursively defined propositions, and a list fold is extracted from an existence theorem (Figure 11.3).

24 theorems, 10 abstractions, checked by replaying their tactic scripts on the kernel. Hover any piece of syntax for its kind, surface form, and uniform term; open Tactics, Proof, or Analysis to go deeper.

-- | Lists as a programming theory, following Constable et al. §11.2
-- (the Nuprl book’s “Lists and Arrays”).
--
-- A discrete type has decidable equality; a predicate is decidable when it
-- or its negation holds at every point. Head is defined in two ways (partial
-- vs. defaulted), tail and length by `list_ind`, membership and
-- non-repetition as recursively defined propositions, and a list fold is
-- extracted from an existence theorem (Figure 11.3).
theory ListProg

comment book "Constable et al. §11.2: lists and arrays as a programming theory."

abs Discrete(T) == ∀x:T. ∀y:T. x = y ∈ T ∨ ¬(x = y ∈ T)
abs Decidable(T; F) == ∀x:T. F x ∨ ¬(F x)
abs Hd(d; l) == list_ind l (d) (h, t, v. h)
abs Tl(l) == list_ind l ([]) (h, t, v. t)
abs Len(l) == list_ind l 0 (h, t, v. v + 1)
abs On(e; l; T) == list_ind l False (h, t, v. (e = h ∈ T) ∨ v)
abs Unique(l; T) == list_ind l True (h, t, v. ¬(On(h; t; T)) ∧ v)
abs Append(xs; ys) == list_ind xs (ys) (h, t, ih. h :: ih)
abs Sum(l) == list_ind l 0 (h, t, v. h + v)
abs Map(f; xs) == list_ind xs ([]) (h, t, ih. f h :: ih)

soft Discrete, Decidable, Hd, Tl, Len, On, Unique, Append, Sum, Map

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Discreteness and decidability
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem int_discrete :
  Discrete(Int)
proof
  intro x
  intro y
  decide x = y THENL [left THEN hyp, right THEN hyp]
qed

theorem unit_discrete :
  Discrete(Unit)
proof
  intro x
  intro y
  left
  eq
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Head with a default (hdd of Figure 11.2)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem hd_nil :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀d:A. Hd(d; []) = d ∈ A
proof
  intro A
  intro d
  eq
qed

theorem hd_cons :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀d:A. ∀h:A. ∀t:List A. Hd(d; h :: t) = h ∈ A
proof
  intro A
  intro d
  intro h
  intro t
  auto
qed

theorem hd_inhab :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀d:A. ∀l:List A. Hd(d; l) ∈ A
proof
  intro A
  intro d
  intro l
  elim 3 THENL [hyp, hyp]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Tail, length, nil discrimination
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem tl_nil :
  ∀A:U{i}. Tl([]) = [] ∈ List A
proof
  intro A
  eq
qed

theorem tl_cons :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀h:A. ∀t:List A. Tl(h :: t) = t ∈ List A
proof
  intro A
  intro h
  intro t
  auto
qed

theorem len_nil :
  Len([]) = 0 ∈ Int
proof
  eq
qed

theorem len_two :
  Len([1, 2]) = 2 ∈ Int
proof
  eq
qed

theorem list_decide_nil :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀l:List A. l = [] ∈ List A ∨ ¬(l = [] ∈ List A)
proof
  intro A
  intro l
  elim 2 THENL [
    left THEN eq,
    right THEN intro p THEN elim 6
  ]
qed

theorem nil_ne_cons :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀h:A. ∀t:List A. ¬([] = h :: t ∈ List A)
proof
  intro A
  intro h
  intro t
  intro p
  elim 4
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Membership (`e on l over T` of §11.2)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem on_nil :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀e:A. ¬(On(e; []; A))
proof
  intro A
  intro e
  intro p
  elim 3
qed

theorem on_cons_head :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀e:A. ∀t:List A. On(e; e :: t; A)
proof
  intro A
  intro e
  intro t
  reduce
  left
  eq
qed

theorem on_cons_tail :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀e:A. ∀h:A. ∀t:List A. On(e; t; A) → On(e; h :: t; A)
proof
  intro A
  intro e
  intro h
  intro t
  intro p
  reduce
  right
  hyp
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Non-repetition
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem unique_nil :
  ∀A:U{i}. Unique([]; A)
proof
  intro A
  intro
qed

theorem unique_cons :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀h:A. ∀t:List A.
    ¬(On(h; t; A)) → Unique(t; A) → Unique(h :: t; A)
proof
  intro A
  intro h
  intro t
  intro n
  intro u
  reduce
  split THENL [hyp, hyp]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Fold / “generalize to list” (Figure 11.3)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The fold of Figure 11.3, specialised to integer sum (the book’s `sum`).
theorem fold_sum_cons :
  list_ind (1 :: 2 :: []) 0 (h, t, ih. h + ih) = 1 + list_ind (2 :: []) 0 (h, t, ih. h + ih) ∈ Int
proof
  eq
qed

theorem sum_nil :
  Sum([]) = 0 ∈ Int
proof
  eq
qed

theorem sum_three :
  Sum([1, 2, 3]) = 6 ∈ Int
proof
  eq
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Append and map
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem append_nil :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀ys:List A. Append([]; ys) = ys ∈ List A
proof
  intro A
  intro ys
  auto
qed

theorem append_cons :
  Append(1 :: []; 2 :: []) = 1 :: 2 :: [] ∈ List Int
proof
  auto
qed

theorem append_assoc_closed :
  Append(Append(1 :: []; 2 :: []); 3 :: []) = Append(1 :: []; Append(2 :: []; 3 :: [])) ∈ List Int
proof
  eq THEN auto
qed

theorem map_nil :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. ∀f:(A → B). Map(f; []) = [] ∈ List B
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro f
  auto
qed

theorem map_add1 :
  Map((λn. n + 1); [0, 1]) = [1, 2] ∈ List Int
proof
  auto
qed
